question:

question:
A netball player pushes off the ground at the ankle joint as they jump to intercept a pass, moving the ankle from a dorsi-flexed position (A) to a fully plantar-flexed position (B) as they leave the ground.

Name, sketch and label the lever system operating at the ankle joint from position A to position B.

(Diagram description: since this website cannot render a hand-drawn sketch, describe the correct layout of the lever system instead.)
markScheme: 2 marks: Second class lever/order (1); correctly labelled in the order fulcrum, load, effort (accept reverse) (1).

question: State one mechanical advantage of the lever system operating at the ankle joint in this movement.
markScheme: 1 mark: Overcomes heavy loads/body weight — a large force is generated due to the longer effort arm, reducing the effort required to lift the body's weight off the ground.

question:
Sprinting is an example of a physical activity that relies on effective lever systems. During the drive phase of sprinting, the right ankle moves from a dorsi-flexed position (A) to a plantar-flexed position (B) as the foot pushes off the track.

State one mechanical advantage and one mechanical disadvantage of the lever system being used at the right ankle during this movement.
markScheme:
2 marks (must be identified as advantage or disadvantage):
Advantage: larger forces generated/longer effort arm, making it easier to move heavy loads/generate high force (sub max 1 mark).
Disadvantage: limited range of movement/limited or reduced speed of movement (sub max 1 mark).
Max 2 marks.

question:
A high jumper is approaching take-off using the Fosbury Flop technique, driving off their left leg to gain height over the bar.

Analyse how the musculoskeletal and lever systems operate at the left knee and ankle to achieve an effective take-off.

(AO1 = 2 marks, AO2 = 3 marks, AO3 = 3 marks)
markScheme:
Indicative content — mark holistically using the levels below.
AO1 may include: the ankle is a hinge joint (talus, tibia, fibula), with the gastrocnemius and tibialis anterior acting at the joint; the knee is a hinge joint (femur, tibia), with the quadriceps and hamstrings acting at the joint; levers consist of a fulcrum, resistance and effort.
AO2 may include: at the ankle, plantar flexion occurs due to concentric contraction of the gastrocnemius (agonist), antagonised by the tibialis anterior, in the sagittal plane around the transverse axis; the lever system at the ankle is a second class lever. At the knee, extension occurs due to concentric contraction of the quadriceps (agonist), antagonised by the hamstrings, also in the sagittal plane around the transverse axis; the lever system at the knee is a third class lever.
AO3 may include: the third class lever at the knee is a mechanical disadvantage (effort arm shorter than load arm) but allows a large range of movement, requiring forceful quadriceps contraction to generate speed; the second class lever at the ankle is a mechanical advantage (effort arm longer than load arm), aiding the drive off the ground, though at the expense of speed of movement; if the jumper sinks into the take-off, the knee and ankle flex further, causing an eccentric contraction of the quadriceps/gastrocnemius under load, followed by a powerful concentric contraction on take-off.
Band 4 (7-8): Detailed, accurate, well-linked analysis across AO1/AO2/AO3.
Band 3 (5-6): Good knowledge and mostly accurate application/analysis.
Band 2 (3-4): Basic knowledge, limited application/analysis.
Band 1 (1-2): Very limited/isolated points.
0 marks: No relevant content.
Max 8 marks.

question: During the recovery phase of front crawl, a third-class lever is operating at the shoulder to allow flexion. Explain the mechanical advantage of the third-class lever operating at the shoulder for the swimmer.
markScheme:
2 marks from:
- (Mechanical advantage) allows a large range of movement/the resistance or load can be moved quickly (1).
- This allows the swimmer to move their arm rapidly through the recovery phase and reposition it quickly for the next stroke, maintaining stroke rate/speed (1).
Max 2 marks.

question: The ankle operates as a lever as a cyclist stands and pushes down hard on the pedal during a steep uphill climb. Identify the class of lever operating at the ankle and explain the mechanical advantage of this class of lever for the cyclist.
markScheme:
3 marks from:
- Second class lever system (1).
- Effort arm (force arm) is longer than the resistance/load arm (1).
- This means the cyclist can generate greater force at the pedal for a given muscular effort, allowing them to overcome the resistance of the incline efficiently (1).
Max 3 marks.

question: A cricketer bowls the ball, extending their arm rapidly from behind the head to release the ball. Name the lever system operating at the elbow during this extension.
markScheme: First class lever (1). Accept description of fulcrum (elbow joint) positioned between the effort (triceps) and the resistance (forearm/hand/ball). Max 1 mark.
